title: Orphaned ImpressedPostsQueryHydrator permanently neuters the README-documented PreviouslySeenPostsBackupFilter
claim: home-mixer/candidate_hydrators's sibling query_hydrators/impressed_posts_query_hydrator.rs (ImpressedPostsQueryHydrator) is fully implemented, module-declared, and constructed inside PhoenixCandidatePipeline::build_with_clients, but its constructor result is bound to an underscore-prefixed local (`_impressed_posts_hydrator`) that is never pushed into the pipeline's query_hydrators Vec passed to the struct. Consequently query.impressed_post_ids is Vec::new() (its Default) for every real request through PhoenixCandidatePipeline. home-mixer/filters/previously_seen_posts_backup_filter.rs -- one of the 17 filters README's own Pre-Scoring Filters table documents as 'The same [previously-seen-post filtering], from a second record of impressions' -- early-returns 'kept: all candidates, removed: none' whenever query.impressed_post_ids.is_empty(). Since that field is always empty under current wiring, this filter is a permanent silent no-op in the current build.

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: query_hydrators Vec construction; `let _impressed_posts_hydrator = ImpressedPostsQueryHydrator { ... };` (never appended to the Vec)
impressed_post_ids: Vec<u64> field and its Vec::new() default in ScoredPostsQuery::new

runtime_caveats: This is confirmed only for PhoenixCandidatePipeline; the other 5 pipelines never reference ImpressedPostsClient/ImpressedPostsQueryHydrator at all, so the same conclusion holds for them by simple absence.
S01 did not verify whether an internal, unpublished build variant re-adds this hydrator; only this exact checked-in snapshot is characterized.
notes: Lens L03 (reachability) textbook case: the hydrator is declared, exported, and constructed, but never reaches the active pipeline Vec -- 'constructed' is not 'wired'. README's Pre-Scoring Filters table (verified structurally accurate in S00) does not distinguish a filter that runs-but-never-matches from one that meaningfully filters; this is a documentation/implementation gap worth flagging to S00's original claim S00-C019 as a correction candidate: the filter is present and unconditionally enabled, but functionally inert given current wiring.

title: Three fully-implemented pipeline components are absent from their module's mod.rs and are not part of the compiled home-mixer crate
claim: home-mixer/sources/popular_topics_source.rs (PopularTopicsSource), home-mixer/filters/popular_topics_author_dedup_filter.rs (PopularTopicsAuthorDedupFilter), and home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/broadcast_liveness_hydrator.rs (BroadcastLivenessHydrator) are each fully implemented (with unit tests) but none is declared via a `pub mod <name>;` line in its directory's mod.rs, and none is referenced anywhere else in home-mixer/. Rust's module system means these three files are not reachable from crate root and are not part of the compiled binary under the current source tree. Independently, two of the three (PopularTopicsSource, BroadcastLivenessHydrator) also hardcode `fn enable(&self, _query: &ScoredPostsQuery) -> bool { false }` -- an unconditional, non-configurable disablement that would apply even if the module declarations were restored.

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: struct PopularTopicsSource; fn enable(...) -> bool { false }
impl Hydrator ... fn enable(&self, query: &ScoredPostsQuery) -> bool { false }
pub broadcast_is_live: Option<bool> -- set exclusively by the orphaned hydrator, so always None at runtime
broadcast_is_live: candidate.broadcast_is_live -- the field's only downstream reader, always forwards None

runtime_caveats: A repository-wide grep for each symbol name confirmed zero other references; this is a structural (module-graph) conclusion, not a build execution, so S01 did not literally compile the crate to double-confirm -- but Rust's `mod`-declaration requirement for a file to be part of a crate is deterministic and not runtime-configurable.

PopularTopicsSource and PopularTopicsAuthorDedupFilter are a matched pair (source + its companion author-dedup filter) suggesting a deliberately paused or reverted 'Popular Topics' candidate-source feature rather than three unrelated oversights.
notes: PopularTopicsSource queries visibility-unfiltered Strato 'popular topic tweets' across 22 hardcoded Grok topic categories (grox_topics::TOPIC_*) -- an entirely undocumented candidate-discovery mechanism, dormant twice over (module-tree absence + hardcoded enable=false). This should be treated as evidence of an in-progress or deliberately shelved feature, not as proof it will never activate -- but activation would require more than restoring the mod.rs declarations and enable() bodies: PopularTopicsSource has no external symbol reference anywhere in the current source tree (unlike S01-F001's ImpressedPostsQueryHydrator, which IS module-declared but still needs its constructor's result added to an active pipeline Vec), so making it live would also require adding construction/wiring into a candidate pipeline's sources Vec and satisfying whatever client/dependency wiring that construction needs. S01 makes no claim about whether/when any of that has happened in an unpublished build.

title: PhoenixCandidatePipeline's constructed candidate-source list has 7 sources, not the 3 README documents; SimClusters wiring is confirmed
claim: The `sources: Vec<Box<dyn Source<ScoredPostsQuery, PostCandidate>>>` constructed in PhoenixCandidatePipeline::build_with_clients contains, in order: ThunderSource (in-network), TweetMixerSource, SimclustersSource, PhoenixSource, PhoenixTopicsSource, PhoenixMOESource, and CachedPostsSource. README's Candidate Sources table and request-path diagram name only Thunder, Phoenix retrieval, and SimClusters. TweetMixerSource, PhoenixTopicsSource, and PhoenixMOESource are constructed, wired into the live pipeline, and eligible to execute when their enable() conditions pass (each has its own gate, none hardcoded false) but are not named anywhere in README.md. Whether any given request actually invokes them depends on those gates -- e.g. TweetMixerSource's enable() requires EnableTweetMixerSource, !query.in_network_only, and !query.has_cached_posts -- so 'wired into the pipeline' establishes reachability, not unconditional execution. This resolves S00-C043: SimClusters is directly confirmed wired as an out-of-network source alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval, exactly as README claims -- but that claim is also incomplete about the other 4 sources.
runtime_caveats: S01 confirmed these three sources exist, are constructed, and have request-dependent (non-hardcoded) enable() gates; S01 did not deep-read their internal retrieval semantics (e.g. what 'MOE' selects, how PhoenixTopicsSource differs from PhoenixSource) -- that belongs to S04/S05/S07 as the retrieval-semantics owners.
Whether any of the 7 sources' checked-in enable() gate defaults are overridden at runtime is a separate, unestablished question (S17).
notes: Corrects/extends S00-C043 (previously PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED/STRONG_INFERENCE pending S01) to CONFIRMED for the SimClusters-specific sub-claim, while surfacing 3 additional undocumented sources as a new, separate documentation-completeness gap the README's Candidate Sources table does not disclose.

title: candidate-pipeline framework resolves S00-F008: per-candidate hydrator/scorer errors are silently absorbed, never drop the candidate or fail the request; per-source errors silently contribute zero candidates
claim: candidate-pipeline/hydrator.rs's and candidate-pipeline/scorer.rs's default `update_all(&self, candidates: &mut [C], results: Vec<Result<C,String>>)` implementations iterate `candidates.iter_mut().zip(results)` and only call `self.update(candidate, value)` `if let Ok(value) = result` -- an Err entry is a silent no-op for that candidate: it is neither dropped from the pipeline nor does it fail the request, it simply keeps whatever field values it already had before that hydrator/scorer ran. Applied to BidirectionalFollowHydrator (S00-F008): when its socialgraph_client call fails, hydrate() returns Err for every candidate, so every candidate's is_mutual_follow_author/author_follows_viewer simply remain at their prior (unset/None) value for that request -- the bidirectional-follow boost becomes a no-op for that request's candidates, but no candidate is removed and the request completes normally. Separately, candidate-pipeline/candidate_pipeline.rs's fetch_candidates() collects `results.into_iter().flatten()` over `Vec<Result<Vec<C>,String>>` from concurrently-run sources: a source returning Err contributes zero candidates and is silently skipped, while other sources' Ok results are unaffected and still merged -- confirming one source's failure coexists with successful results from others.

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: run_hydrators -- shared by hydrate() and hydrate_post_selection()
hydrate() error path returning Err for every candidate

runtime_caveats: Query hydrators (a separate trait) follow an analogous but distinct pattern in candidate_pipeline.rs's hydrate_query/hydrate_dependent_query: `if let Ok(hydrated) = result { hydrator.update(&mut hydrated_query, hydrated); }` -- same silent-skip semantics, one query object rather than per-candidate.

A hydrator/scorer that returns a Vec of the wrong length triggers a length-mismatch guard in the trait's default run() wrapper, converting the ENTIRE batch to Err for every candidate in that stage invocation -- still governed by the same silent-skip update_all semantics, so this defensive guard does not escalate to a request failure either.
notes: This is the single most consequential piece of orchestration-framework semantics S01 established: no per-candidate or per-source failure in the hydration/scoring/retrieval stages can fail a request outright; failures degrade data quality (stale/missing fields, fewer candidates) rather than availability. Filters have no fallibility at the trait level at all (Filter::filter returns a total FilterResult partition, not a Result). Side effects are separately and even more completely isolated from the response: they run via tokio::spawn with results explicitly discarded (candidate-pipeline/candidate_pipeline.rs's run_side_effects, `let _ = join_all(futures).await;`), so no side-effect failure can affect the response under any circumstance.

title: Concurrency is stage-specific, not uniform: hydrator/source stages run concurrently, filters and scorers run strictly sequentially, the selector is a single synchronous call, and side effects run concurrently inside a fire-and-forget spawn
claim: candidate-pipeline/candidate_pipeline.rs's execute_stages() does not apply one concurrency model uniformly; each stage type has its own, confirmed directly from source: query hydrators run concurrently (tokio join_all over all enabled hydrators, hydrate_query); dependent query hydrators run concurrently, after all base query hydrators complete (hydrate_dependent_query); sources run concurrently (fetch_candidates); candidate hydrators run concurrently (hydrate, via the shared run_hydrators helper); pre-scoring filters run strictly SEQUENTIALLY in declared array order (run_filters is a plain for-loop, not join_all): each filter narrows the exact candidate Vec the next filter receives; scorers run strictly SEQUENTIALLY in declared array order (the for-loop in score()): each scorer's update_all mutates the shared candidate slice before the next scorer runs, so a later scorer can in principle read a field an earlier scorer just set; the selector is a single synchronous invocation (select()), not a set of concurrent components at all; post-selection hydrators run concurrently, on the already-selected candidate set only (hydrate_post_selection, same run_hydrators helper); post-selection filters run strictly SEQUENTIALLY (filter_post_selection, same run_filters helper); side effects: the ENABLED side effects execute concurrently with each other (tokio join_all) but the whole group runs inside a single fire-and-forget tokio::spawn dispatched after the response's final_candidates are already computed -- so side-effect concurrency is real among themselves but happens entirely after, and independently of, response finalization. The material conclusion this establishes: filter and scorer execution order is directly, causally behaviorally significant -- not merely a documentation convenience -- because those two stage types are the only ones where a component's output can depend on a same-stage predecessor's output. This confirms and refines README's implicit ordering and resolves S00-C045 (whether README's 7-stage diagram reflects true source execution order): the diagram's high-level stage sequence (query hydration -> sources -> candidate hydration -> pre-scoring filters -> scoring -> selection -> post-selection hydration+filters) is DIRECTLY correct, but the diagram does not distinguish concurrent from strictly-sequential sub-execution within stages, and collapses the post-selection hydrator stage (VFCandidateHydrator, concurrent, selected candidates only) and the post-selection filter stage (VFFilter/AncillaryVFFilter/DedupConversationFilter, sequential) into one informal grouping.

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: score -- imperative for-loop over scorers, no join_all
scorers: Vec = vec![phoenix_scorer, ranking_scorer, vm_ranker] -- declared order is the executed order

runtime_caveats: Whether any specific scorer in PhoenixCandidatePipeline's 3-scorer chain (PhoenixScorer -> RankingScorer -> VMRanker) actually reads a field an earlier scorer set (beyond the well-known score-composition relationship already documented in README) was not individually re-verified per scorer in S01; that is S05/S08 territory.
notes: Supersedes S00-C045's DEFERRED/UNKNOWN status with a DIRECT resolution.

title: 'Blending Pipeline wraps Post Pipeline' is peer-source composition via a synchronous in-process await, not nested pipeline embedding
claim: ForYouCandidatePipeline does not extend, call into, or otherwise structurally embed PhoenixCandidatePipeline's CandidatePipeline trait implementation. Instead, ForYouCandidatePipeline is a fully independent CandidatePipeline<ScoredPostsQuery, FeedItem> instance with its own query hydrators (2, vs. PhoenixCandidatePipeline's 17), its own 7 sources, its own selector (BlenderSelector, not TopKScoreSelector), and its own side effects. One of its 7 sources, ScoredPostsSource, directly calls `self.scored_posts_server.run_pipeline(query.clone()).await`, which itself directly calls `self.phoenix_candidate_pipeline.execute(query).await` -- an ordinary, synchronous, fully-awaited in-process Rust function call (not an RPC to a separate service), whose ScoredPost results are converted to FeedItems and returned as this one source's contribution. The other 6 ForYouCandidatePipeline sources (AdsSource, WhoToFollowSource, PromptsSource, PushToHomeSource, JetfuelFrameSource, FeedSurveySource) are evaluated concurrently alongside this nested Phoenix execution -- each still subject to its own enable() gate, so 'concurrent' describes the execution model for whichever of them are enabled on a given request, not unconditional execution -- and ForYouCandidatePipeline has zero scorers (`fn scorers() -> &[] {}`) -- confirming DIRECTLY that ads/WTF/prompts/etc. are never scored by the Phoenix model; they are merged with the already-fully-ranked organic posts purely via BlenderSelector's interleaving logic. The identical pattern (a Source that awaits a whole separate pipeline's execute()) is reused by RankedFollowingCandidatePipeline (via ScoredPostsSource, same PhoenixCandidatePipeline) and by FollowingCandidatePipeline (via ReverseChronPostsSource, wrapping the separate, unscored ReverseChronPostsPipeline).
runtime_caveats: The two ScoredPostsQuery instances involved (ForYouCandidatePipeline's own query and the clone passed into PhoenixCandidatePipeline) are the same Rust type but populated by two independent, non-overlapping query-hydration passes (2 hydrators at the ForYou level, 17 at the Phoenix level); S01 did not trace every individual field to confirm which ones are actually visible/meaningful at each layer.
notes: Resolves S00-C044. 'Wraps' remains a fair plain-English description of the observable effect (Phoenix's ranked posts do end up inside the For You response alongside ads/WTF/prompts) but is architecturally imprecise: there is no pipeline subclassing/inheritance, only one pipeline's fully-materialized output being consumed as another pipeline's Source.

title: All six S00-identified unplaced filter modules are constructed and active in pipelines other than PhoenixCandidatePipeline; none are orphaned

S01 traced all six to their actual pipelines: AdAdjacentServedFilter -> ForYouCandidatePipeline post_selection_filters; PushToHomeDedupFilter -> ForYouCandidatePipeline (pre-selection) filters; FollowingRetweetDeduplicationFilter and SelfReplyChainFilter -> ReverseChronPostsPipeline filters; InvalidConversationModuleFilter -> FollowingCandidatePipeline filters; ResultSizeFilter -> PhoenixScoresPipeline post_selection_filters. All six are unconditionally enabled (no enable() override in any of the six).

title: An account-status signal from Gizmoduck can silently force in_network_only=true regardless of the client's requested value
claim: home-mixer/server.rs's QueryBuilder::build computes `let in_network_only = proto_query.in_network_only || viewer_data.allow_for_you_recommendations == Some(false);` -- i.e. if the Gizmoduck-sourced ViewerData for the requesting user has allow_for_you_recommendations explicitly set to false, the request is forced into in-network-only mode (no out-of-network/algorithmic recommendations) regardless of what the client application requested. This is a real, account-level eligibility gate on out-of-network content distribution, applied identically across every endpoint that calls QueryBuilder::build (ScoredPosts, ForYou, RankedFollowing, Following, PhoenixScores), and is not documented anywhere in README.md.

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: QueryBuilder::build -- viewer_data fetch and in_network_only computation

runtime_caveats: S01 did not trace what sets allow_for_you_recommendations=false on the Gizmoduck side (that service is external/unpublished) or under what account conditions (enforcement action, user setting, legal/geo restriction, etc.) it becomes false -- only that home-mixer honors it as an unconditional override when present.

The Gizmoduck fetch itself has a 200ms timeout and fails open to ViewerData::default() (see home-mixer/server.rs:L225-L235) -- meaning allow_for_you_recommendations defaults to whatever ViewerData::default() specifies on timeout/error; S01 did not confirm that default's value from this file alone.
notes: Materially relevant to lenses L06/L07/L09: this is an account-state-driven mode switch on out-of-network content eligibility, applied before any pipeline stage runs, for reasons outside the viewer's own request. S01 did not individually verify each out-of-network source's (Phoenix retrieval, SimClusters, TweetMixer, PhoenixTopics, PhoenixMOE) own enable() body to confirm which, if any, explicitly gate on query.in_network_only versus relying on some other downstream exclusion mechanism -- TweetMixerSource is the one source S01 confirmed checks it directly (its enable() requires EnableTweetMixerSource, !query.in_network_only, and !query.has_cached_posts); the practical effect on the other four is a plausible but unverified inference (STRONG_INFERENCE at best), not a DIRECT claim, and is a concrete downstream item for S04/S05/S07. Whether allow_for_you_recommendations=false itself reflects an enforcement mechanism, a user-facing setting, or something else is UNKNOWN from this snapshot and should be routed to whichever specialist can trace Gizmoduck/account-state semantics.

title: Five registered gRPC services are backed by six candidate pipeline implementations; README documents only the two composing the For You feed
claim: home-mixer/server.rs's HomeMixerServer registers five tonic gRPC services -- ScoredPostsService, ForYouFeedService, RankedFollowingFeedService, FollowingFeedService, and PhoenixScoresService -- backed by six distinct CandidatePipeline implementations (PhoenixCandidatePipeline, ForYouCandidatePipeline, RankedFollowingCandidatePipeline, FollowingCandidatePipeline, ReverseChronPostsPipeline, PhoenixScoresPipeline). README.md documents the request path for the For You feed (PhoenixCandidatePipeline + ForYouCandidatePipeline) in detail but does not mention RankedFollowingFeedService, FollowingFeedService/ReverseChronPostsPipeline (a non-ranked, PassthroughSelector, reverse-chronological pipeline), or PhoenixScoresService (which takes explicit seed_candidate_post_ids rather than retrieving candidates, uses PassthroughSelector and a result_size of 2800, and appears to be a bulk/raw scoring API rather than a feed-ranking surface).

pub mod declarations for all 6 pipelines
const RESULT_SIZE: usize = 2800; sources: [SeedCandidatesSource]; selector: PassthroughSelector
query.in_network_only = true forced at the RankedFollowingFeedService and FollowingFeedService server layer

title: A hardcoded 2-user-ID bypass short-circuits pipeline execution entirely, consistently across all five servers
claim: params::TEST_USER_IDS (checked-in as &[123, 234] per S00) is checked at the very top of the pipeline-invoking method in all five server structs -- ScoredPostsServer::run_pipeline, ForYouFeedServer::get_for_you_feed, FollowingFeedServer::get_following_feed, RankedFollowingFeedServer::get_ranked_following_feed, and PhoenixScoresServer::run_pipeline -- each returning an empty result immediately without constructing a query beyond what QueryBuilder::build already produced, without executing any pipeline stage, and without running any side effects.
runtime_caveats: The checked-in value is exactly 2 user IDs (123, 234); this pattern is presumably for synthetic/canary load or infra health checks, not a general testing framework, given how narrowly hardcoded it is.
notes: A genuine 'special query state' per the task's Section A prompt -- the only one S01 found that is keyed on a hardcoded, checked-in user-ID allowlist rather than a request field or account attribute.

title: Debug RPC endpoints accept caller-supplied feature-switch overrides applied directly to the live request
claim: home-mixer/server.rs's get_debug_scored_posts, get_debug_for_you_feed, get_debug_for_you_feed_urt, get_debug_ranked_following_feed, get_debug_following_feed, and get_debug_phoenix_scores handlers all extract `debug_query.feature_switch_overrides` from the incoming request and pass it as `fs_overrides` into QueryBuilder::build, which applies each key/value pair via `results.override_fs(key, value)` directly onto the Params used for that request's entire pipeline execution -- a real, production-code-confirmed per-request feature-switch override mechanism reachable via an RPC parameter, not merely an internal test harness.

six get_debug_* handlers, each threading fs_overrides from the request into QueryBuilder::build

runtime_caveats: S01 did not establish this endpoint's authentication/authorization boundary (e.g. whether get_debug_* RPCs are gated to internal callers only at the gRPC/network layer) -- that is outside this file and outside S01's assigned files.

b3_info.force_sample() is also called on every debug_* path, forcing trace sampling; combined with fs_override, a caller of a debug endpoint can materially change both the executed configuration and its observability for that one request.

title: VMRanker's per-candidate score updates are skipped on whole-call RPC failure; the request continues without VMRanker's contribution rather than failing
claim: home-mixer/scorers/vm_ranker.rs's VMRanker::score, on either xDS or DNS/gRPC call failure to the VMRanker service, returns `vec![Err(msg); candidates.len()]` for the whole batch. Per the framework's default Scorer::update_all semantics (S01-F004, candidate-pipeline/scorer.rs:L50-L56), an Err entry means `self.update(candidate, scored)` is never called for that candidate, so none of VMRanker's per-candidate field updates are applied when the whole call fails. execute_stages() does not fail or halt -- it proceeds to the next stage (select()) with whatever score fields the candidates already carried from the prior stage. This directly establishes that a whole-call VMRanker failure is all-or-nothing (either every candidate gets VMRanker's update or none do) and cannot fail the request.
runtime_caveats: S01 did NOT trace the exact score field(s) RankingScorer writes, whether VMRanker would overwrite that same field on success, PostCandidate's score-representation, or TopKScoreSelector's comparison logic (candidate-pipeline/selector.rs's default score()/sort() vs any override) -- so this finding does not establish, as DIRECT, the stronger downstream claim that 'candidates therefore keep RankingScorer's score' or that 'TopKScoreSelector necessarily uses RankingScorer's ordering' on a VMRanker failure. That specific consequence is STRONG_INFERENCE at best, consistent with the declared 3-scorer sequence (PhoenixScorer -> RankingScorer -> VMRanker, S01-F005) but not independently confirmed field-by-field in S01.

Tracing the exact field-level consequence (which score field TopKScoreSelector reads, and whether VMRanker's success path overwrites vs. supplements RankingScorer's value) is a concrete downstream obligation for S05/S08.
notes: Concrete instance of the general framework failure semantics in S01-F004, specific to a named, documented component (VMRanker / vm-ranker/ service).

title: Boot-time client construction is fail-hard (panics via .expect()) almost everywhere across S01's assigned pipeline/server constructors; ThunderCapiClient is the only graceful-degradation exception found in that sweep
claim: Across PhoenixCandidatePipeline::prod, ForYouCandidatePipeline::new, FollowingCandidatePipeline::new, RankedFollowingCandidatePipeline::new, ReverseChronPostsPipeline::new, PhoenixScoresPipeline::prod, and HomeMixerServer::build, essentially every client constructor is wrapped in `.expect("Failed to create ... client")`, meaning a single failing dependency during process startup panics the entire home-mixer process. Within this bounded sweep -- the 7 boot-time constructor functions across S01's 227 assigned files, each read in full (see S01_run.md for the exact line ranges and method) -- the only exception found is ThunderCapiClient in PhoenixCandidatePipeline::prod, which is constructed via an explicit match that logs a warning and substitutes None (triggering a documented 'proxy path' fallback in ThunderSource) rather than panicking. This claim is bounded to S01's assigned files; boot-time client construction elsewhere in the repository (e.g. within thunder/, phoenix/, or other components outside S01's ownership) was not examined and is not covered by this finding.

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: ProdThunderCapiClient::new match arm -- graceful None fallback with warning
tokio::join! block -- ~30 other client futures each using .expect(...)

runtime_caveats: This is standard, arguably intentional 'fail fast at boot rather than serve broken' design for a service that presumably runs behind orchestrated restarts/health checks; S01 records it as a structural asymmetry worth downstream awareness (S18), not as a defect.
notes: Relevant to L15 (load shedding) and B10 (failure/degraded modes) framing: request-time failures in this codebase are overwhelmingly designed to degrade gracefully (S01-F004), while startup-time failures are overwhelmingly designed to crash-and-restart -- two different failure philosophies applied at two different lifecycle points.
